context: A uni student debriefs a teen friend after a school incident
purpose: Teach: 襲っ/咲き/外人/野郎/クン/ヶ所/はてな/エキサイト

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 先輩、今日の朝、登校中にいきなり犬に襲って来られたんです。
lines.en: Senpai, this morning on the way to school a dog just suddenly came at me.
lines.style: Fast intake of breath. Words tumbling out — trying to get the story out before emotion catches up. Shaken but holding it together. Slight tremor under the surface.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: え、無事?二ヶ所くらい怪我してない?
lines.en: Are you okay? Did it get you anywhere?
lines.style: Sharp concern cutting through. Leans forward. Scans her automatically. Question marks hanging in the air — he's already running through worst-case scenarios.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 幸い無事です。通りすがりの外人さんが助けてくれて。
lines.en: Lucky for me I'm fine. A foreign guy who was passing by stepped in and helped.
lines.style: Exhale of relief. Lighter now, but still grounded. Gratitude settling into her words. The briefest softness when she mentions the stranger.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 良かった。エキサイトしてた野郎、見つかったの?
lines.en: Thank god. Did they manage to catch the dog?
lines.style: Steady, practical. Already moving past fear into problem-solving. Direct — the senpai in him taking over. Warm but efficient.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はてな顔で逃げて行ったみたいで、まだ。
lines.en: Apparently it just bolted, confused or panicked. Still out there somewhere.
lines.style: Quiet, matter-of-fact. She's downplaying it now that danger has passed. Small shrug in her voice. Fading slightly at the end — moving on.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 警察には届けた?「○○クン襲撃事件」みたいに、しっかり名前付けて報告しよ。
lines.en: You should file a report with the police. Get it on the record properly so they can actually track it.
lines.style: Authoritative without being bossy. This is what needs to happen. Speaks with the weight of someone who's thought it through in real time. Firm but protective.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 今日のうちに行きます。桜が咲き始めた季節に、こんなのって…。
lines.en: I'll go today. Right when the cherry blossoms are starting to bloom… of all times.
lines.style: Voice wavers slightly on the opening. Soft sadness threading through — not about the dog itself, but the dissonance of violence in a gentle season. Trailing off into something almost poetic, almost fragile.
